pull_request.body:
## What

`docs/design/github-owner-login-attribution.md` v1 — the P1 design note of `docs/design/evaluation-response-plan-2026-09-24.md` (§4 P1; issues #82, #69). **Class (a)** under agent-rules 12: it governs how the Worker writes the WHO of GitHub webhook events, adds project-policy fields (`github.shared_logins`, `github.identities`) and proposes an environment rule (appendix A, agent-ops 19). Design gate: Codex → NOOA → the Grok seat; the author (claude-code) does not sit.

## Why

Every seat runs `gh` as the repository owner, so the webhook seals every agent's PR open, push, body edit, comment, review and merge as `human` / `github:jordandru` — 650 events at 2026-09-26T03:44Z. The ledger cannot say which of them are Jordan's.

## The design in one paragraph

For a login the project policy marks **shared**, the adapter never writes `type: human`. It writes the **account** (`system` / `github:<login>`) unless exactly one seat's pinned, producer-verified declaration event — logged before the `gh` call, naming the body sha256 / pushed sha / merge commit — matches the payload's content: then the seat (`seat_declared`). Two declarers → `conflicting`; none → `unresolved`; read failure → `unavailable`. The decision is sealed hash-covered in `method.params.owner_login_decision`. Existing events are labelled at read time and amended one at a time only (Jordan's Q4). Per-seat GitHub Apps mapped by `github.identities` are the prevention (step 5), and the shared mark comes off on measured absence of seat use (step 6).

## Evidence behind it

A probe over the export bundle (generated 2026-09-24T18:07:55Z, seq 0–7697; script `~/.retrace/handoff-2026-09-26/probe-owner-login.py`, sha256 `0cf23d48630ac967…`): 576 human `github:jordandru` events in that slice; a pinned event naming the same PR number within ±10 min exists for 546 of them, but for 417 more than one seat names it. Proximity finds the PR, not the hand on `gh` — so evidence is bound to content, not time (§1.3). 49 pinned events already describe a `gh` action in prose and 14 carry `body_sha256`; §3.2 is that practice made a schema.

## Decisions the note asks the gate to confirm

D1–D5 in §0; open questions in §12 (immediate `unavailable` seal vs pending; the 30-minute window; `on_behalf_of` on a `seat_declared` actor; whether v7 amendments admit a `pr:` target; one App per seat).

## Provenance

- Q1–Q4 presented `evt_e5ce6a0ed09e40bc8cd39b57b8801ecf`; Jordan: "Accept all four, draft the P1 note" `evt_603025a3932a4193a23f16b49b742f96`.
- Edits `evt_805c1eb01aaa41cc825bfdb3927bb076` (v1) and `evt_d07fd3beb99e4cd299377e67d12ae661` (fix, head `57299cf`) (declaring this very pull request showed that `pr_open` has no PR number before the call; §3.2 now says so). Base `a39cf91`.
- This pull request was declared before `gh pr create` under the note's own §3.2: the declaration event names this body's normalised sha256 and the head sha, and the outcome event names the PR number — a live sample for T3.
